messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 502/504s observed on prod-gateway in us-east-1. 5xx_rate=6.8% over 90s, p95 latency increased. Paging primary oncall.

alex: I'm on it. grabbing dashboards and k8s events. any deploys in the last 20m? :mag:

maya: Edge team did a TLS/SNI routing tweak at 15:48 UTC to support new cdn certs (cfg: sni-route-2026-04-10). Could be related.

sam: LB metrics show a surge of CONNECT failures between proxy -> gateway cluster starting 15:49. seeing many upstream resets (RST) and TLS handshake alerts in envoy logs.

ravi: tokenizer svc healthy per k8s but I see connection resets on incoming sockets. can someone paste a sample envoy log? guessing SNI mismatch sending traffic to wrong cluster.

alex: pasting snippet from envoy (gateway-proxy-5):
```
[2026-04-10T15:50:12Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 - upstream_reset_before_response: reset reason=connection_failure, peer_address=10.12.3.9:8080, requested_server_name="api.redwood.net"
[2026-04-10T15:50:12Z] TLS alert (handshake failure) from 10.12.3.9
```

maya: confirm: the new SNI mapping accidentally directed some traffic to the legacy admin endpoint which expects client certs -> backend closes connection (TLS alert). that would cause gateway -> upstream reset -> 502.

ravi: yep, tokenizer pods are fine but requests that hit admin endpoint are dropped. can we roll the SNI mapping back? ops?

ops-bot: rollback job queued: reverting cfg sni-route-2026-04-10 -> sni-route-2026-04-09 (initiated by alex). ETA 30s.

alex: initiating quick mitigation steps: 1) rollback SNI mapping, 2) enable gateway rate limiter to throttle new sessions to tokenizer to reduce pressure, 3) switch failing host header to fallback cluster.

sam: applied rate limit at gateway: `envoy: route.match: prefix "/v1/" : max_connections=2000, connection_limit_action=external_mitigate`. watching.

cs-bot: CS note: we see a spike in tickets referencing 502s for /v1/generate from enterprise customers in us-east. open cases: CS-19555, CS-19556. Estimated impacted requests: ~12k last 20m.

maya: rollback completed at 15:51:05 UTC. SNI now points to correct pool. verifying.

ravi: after rollback, upstream resets drop dramatically. tokenizer trace shows successful handshakes to port 8080 now. logs:
```
2026-04-10T15:51:14Z tokenizer-2: accepted TLS handshake from 10.14.9.3
2026-04-10T15:51:15Z tokenizer-2: processed request id=abc123 latency=85ms
```

alex: metrics—5xx rate fell from 6.8% -> 1.3% within 90s of rollback + rate-limit. p95 latency trending down. good.

sam: follow-up mitigation: adding a validation gate to the CDN/edge rollout pipeline to detect SNI routing mismatches (preflight probe that checks TLS servername and expected backend cert). recommending a staged rollout by region.

maya: agree. also adding a canary flag that directs 1% traffic to new SNI mapping for 30m before full rollout.

ravi: tokenizer team will add defensive handling: respond with a clearly identified 421/495 if TLS client auth required, so gateway can triage more clearly instead of generic resets.

ops-bot: action tasks created: OP-4721 (add SNI preflight tests), OP-4722 (canary rollout policy), OP-4723 (gateway response mapping for TLS failures). Assigned to infra and edge.

cs-bot: Customer comms: templated message sent to affected accounts. High-touch customers contacted by CS lead. ETA follow-ups 45-90m.

alex: declaring incident contained at 15:53 UTC. continuing to monitor for 30m. handing to maya for post-incident work and RCA.

maya: Handoff ack. next steps I'll own:
- gather traces and full request ids for 15:45-16:00 window
- run SNI/Envoy mapping audit and produce a roll-out checklist
- coordinate with CDN provider for safer certificate/SNI updates
- validate gateway logic to expose TLS failure reason in metrics

ravi: tokenizer will add better logs for TLS/auth errors and a small fix to return explicit HTTP 495/496 where appropriate. planning patch v2.5.4 in next 4 hours.

alex: great. leaving channel. ping me if it bubbles back up. nice quick rollback everyone. :rocket:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2. Duration (containment): ~8m. Please complete postmortem and link OP tasks.
